key_insight: Auxiliary entanglement, quantified by Schmidt rank, sets a sharp threshold for how well two-photon photonic Bell states can be identified in higher-dimensional qudit systems.
engineering_relevance: This provides a design rule for quantum networking and fusion-based photonic hardware: higher Bell-measurement capability requires auxiliary resources with rank at least ceil(d/2) for partial identification and rank d for deterministic discrimination.
method: Proves an exact auxiliary Schmidt-rank threshold for embedded Bell measurements on two photons carrying qudits of dimension d.
Shows single conclusive Bell-labeling becomes possible at r_Φ ≥ ceil(d/2).
Shows complete deterministic Bell-state discrimination of all d² labels requires r_Φ ≥ d, achievable with a maximally entangled rank-d auxiliary state.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports a theoretical proof with exact resource bounds, rather than an empirical dataset or numerical evaluation.
watch_item: The result is a resource threshold, but practical implementation still depends on realizing sufficiently high-rank auxiliary entanglement and compatible photonic mode sorting with low loss.
paper_title: Auxiliary Schmidt Rank as a Resource for Photonic Bell Measurements
